title: Allbirds Strikes A Classic Cord With New Collection
summary: Timeless material is the finishing touch to the footwear brand’s seasonal styles.
body_markdown:
**SAN FRANCISCO, December 3, 2024** – Allbirds is tapping into nostalgia by adding an iconic heritage material to its library: corduroy. For the first time, Allbirds reimagined two silhouettes–the Runner Go and Lounger Lift–with the seasonal staple, just in time to take its rightful place in winter wardrobes.


The Corduroy collection styles are constructed with 100% organic cotton, divided into “wales” (thick threads) that give corduroy’s signature striped effect. This material adds novelty and nostalgia to any outfit, with durability, warmth, and texture that make corduroy a true feel good fabric. Styles are available in Stony Beige and Natural Black, offering an undeniably relaxed yet polished look.


In a culture where fashion trends rise and decline faster than ever, corduroy has withstood the test of time. This cold weather classic arrives year after year, transcending generations thanks to new applications – from overalls, to pants, to shoes – and enduring comfort.


The Corduroy collection delivers exactly that, thanks to a padded heel collar and wool-lined insole for a soft, snug and supportive fit; and a cushioned, cloud-like SweetFoam® midsole for an ultra-supportive feel underfoot.


The styles are available online and in-store beginning December 3, 2024. The Corduroy Runner Go ($120) is available in full- and half-sizes from W5-11 and M7-14; and the women’s-only Corduroy Lounger Lift ($110) is available in full-sizes from W5-11.


**About Allbirds, Inc.**


Based in San Francisco, with its roots in New Zealand, Allbirds launched in 2016 with a single shoe: the now iconic Wool Runner. In the years since, Allbirds has sold millions of pairs of shoes, and has maintained its commitment to incredible comfort, versatile style and unmatched quality. This is made possible with materials like Allbirds’s sugarcane-based midsole technology, SweetFoam™, and textiles made with tree fibers and Merino wool – so consumers don't have to compromise between the best products and their impact on the earth.[www.allbirds.com](http://www.allbirds.com/)
